report_1.original_text:
75-year-old patient, hypertensive on therapy, overweight, previous prostate cancer excision (2012) with normal follow-up. Severe allergy to insect venom (always carries adrenaline), taking Bactrim and OKI (Kestine as needed). Reports no allergy to ASA (but never PERSONS_NAME). Reports recent cardiology check-up ok. Reports familly history of endorbital neoplasia (RELATIVE).
About 10 days ago in the evening, sudden pain in the left supraorbital region. The next morning, evidence of diplopia when looking down and outwards, stable during the day, persistent in the following days for which patient went to Ophthalmic Hospital Emergency Department: given therapy with eye drops (netilmicin/dexamethasone), which the patient applied regularly with no apparent improvement, for which yesterday 01/24 a new outpatient eye examination was carried out: no findings were reported in the orthoptic evaluation, neurological evaluation and MRI were recommended. In recent days, concomitant finding of high blood pressure values, for which antihypertensive therapy was adjusted (addition of amlodipine 5 mg in the evening; patient already takes olprezide 40/25). Thus today's visit to the Emergency Department.
CT brain + eye sockets not significant, CBC + CRP nothing to note, HGT 78.
Upon neurological examination, blurred edges in the leftwards gaze, as well as in the outwards vertical left, no evident ophthalmoparesis, reduced DTR in altered release, the rest within normal limits.
In Conclusions: trochlear nerve palsy, now apparently resolved, due to uncompensated hypertension. A baseline brain MRI to rule out small lacuna, Doppler ultrasound of the supra-aortic vessels, and lipid profile assessment would be useful given the patient's risk profile. Thyroid function normal at recent check-up. I would wait until the results of the prescribed tests are available before starting antiplatelet therapy, especially considering the patient's severe allergic diathesis.

APR-2013 Subarachnoid hemorrhage, arterial hypertension, senile dementia, total left hip prosthesis, hypothyroidism 
Patient has been unable to walk for two years

report_4.original_text:
72-year-old male, family history, former smoker, arterial hypertension, obesity.
CAD note: 11/30/2021 hospitalization in cardiology to perform coronary angiography for suspected exertional angina (for some time angina and dyspnea upon exertion), in addition, from 11/23/2021 finding of AF, dabigatran started.
Coronary angiogram procedure shows triple vessel CAD: critical diminished DX, chronic occlusion of marginal branches, ulcerated lesion on 70% of middle LAD, after initiation of DAPT (ASA + clopidogrel), PTCA + 1 DES on middle LAD.
Echocardiogram, shows overall kinesis preserved, infero-basal akinesia, moderate pericardial effusion, max 18 mm in posterolateral site, organized, no tamponade. Not on NAO. Follow-up visit at three months.
Sent to Emergency Department after cardiological evaluation for worsening peripheral edema associated with dyspnea over past few months.  
in past medical history: arterial hypertension, in 2018 subtotal colectomy for adenocarcinoma of the rectum followed by a cycle of FOLFOX chemotherapy
post-operative incisional hernia
Regular follow-up
Tx:  losartan 100 1 tablet, nebilox 5 mg , ferrograd, lasix 25 mg omeprazen , asa 1 tablet, lasitone, atorvastatin , clopidogrel 75.
At the time of the visit, the patient reports dyspnea upon mild exertion since discharge with PDN, no angina.
Marked peripheral EDEMA, turgor of the jugulars, apparent Killip 1, BP 160/90 mmHg, HR 89, SO2: 96%.
Arrhythmic tones, no murmurs.
FAST scan shows severe organized pericardial effusion, max at lateral site (about 30-33 mm) with deposition of echodense material on the visceral pericardium, about 18 mm in front of right V (without collapse of the right cavities), IVC 20 mm, collapsed.
Another echocardiogram at the clinic with Doppler evaluation would be useful, possible hemodynamic impact, even if the IVC does not appear severely dilated).
Patient in AF, creat 1.6 mg/dl, should be started on NOA (after evaluation of pericardial effusion), after echocardiogram evaluate whether to start clexane 6000 X 2
